title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-12

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording captures a high‑energy 1968 show with standout Dark Star, The Eleven and an electrifying Other One despite the lack of Pigpen’s organ.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers crystal‑clear stereo soundboard quality with crisp drum separation, though a slightly high percussion level can be distracting. Musically the concert shines – the first set boasts a classic Dark Star, tight The Eleven and powerful Death Don't Have No Mercy, while the second set offers an inspiring Other One suite and Phil’s soaring New Potato solo, even if Pigpen’s organ is noticeably absent.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance (multiple 5‑star comments on Dark Star, The Eleven, Other One, etc.) and recording quality (excellent soundboard with minor mix quirks) across six detailed reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo soundboard with crisp clarity and excellent drum panning; some reviewers note percussion/guisro high in the mix and a slightly distracting level, but overall the audio is superb.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is regarded as stronger with tight jams and smooth transitions; second set remains energetic but suffers from a rough New Potato transition and the absence of Pigpen’s organ, making the overall flow slightly uneven.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Great vocal performance on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy; guitar tone praised as excellent.
band_member_comments.Phil: His Thirteens‑style solo during New Potato is described as astonishing and a highlight of the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal work noted as nice, especially on New Potato and Saint Stephen.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ absent throughout, making the keyboard presence noticeably missing; some mention keyboards high in the mix but generally the lack of organ is felt.
band_member_comments.Drums: Weak drums mentioned early in the second set; percussion panned well stereo‑wise but a guiro/percussion element sits high in the mix for some listeners.
